name: The World of AI: Robotics Models catalogue from Hugging Face Hub
title: The World of AI: Robotics Models catalogue from Hugging Face Hub
answer: The World of AI publishes a Robotics Models catalogue page listing the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. It says the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The most useful point for AI in Transportation is that vision-language-action models are tracked in this catalogue, giving a dated, source-linked view of open robotics models that may support transportation robotics work.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page. It is a catalogue of the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The page states it was last verified on 2026-09-27 and that its source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads. Every model links to its own Hub page. The page also carries site-wide text about searching published pages, books by Stephen R. Jordan, SRJ Consulting & Services, audits and assessments, and a novel, The AI Lawyer.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents a Robotics Models catalogue. Its main claim is that it lists the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. It repeats that description and begins a phrase about vision-language-action models, though the supplied text cuts off there. The page says its source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, refreshed daily, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It states a last verified date of 2026-09-27. Beyond the catalogue, the page describes a search function covering the full text of every published page, all built from the same database. That database includes state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests. The page also promotes books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, and says SRJ Consulting & Services has published its first work of fiction on AI, The AI Lawyer, a novel, out 17 August 2026. It lists audits and assessments such as the AI Business Enablement Audit, the AI Readiness & Performance Assessment, and the AI Risk & Governance Review. It describes itself as an atlas of artificial intelligence covering what the law says and who is suing whom, with every page rebuilt daily from primary sources and carrying its last verified date.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the catalogue covers the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. It says the source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It gives a last verified date of 2026-09-27. It names vision-language-action models, though the phrase is cut off. It also states that The AI Lawyer novel is out 17 August 2026 and that the site is free to read, free to cite, and free to query.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Transportation can use this source as a dated catalogue of open robotics models, including vision-language-action models, with licence and download signals. It does not discuss transportation, but it provides a source-linked list of models that may be relevant to robotics work in the sector. Because it is refreshed daily and links to each model's Hub page, it can help a reader check what open robotics models are most downloaded and what licences apply before investigating them further. It is a discovery tool rather than an assessment of performance or fit for transportation use.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Transportation

sections.body: The source is a catalogue page with limited descriptive text, not an analysis or evaluation. It covers only the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, sorted by all-time downloads, so it excludes closed models, models not on that Hub, and models outside that download ranking. It does not cover transportation applications, performance, safety, or deployment. The supplied text is truncated at vision-language-action, so the page's full description of those models is not available here. The page also carries promotional material for books, consulting services, audits, and a novel, so it is partly commercial. It is dated 2026-09-27 and says it is refreshed daily.
